details: CONFIRMED. stored() keeps (batch costUsd, number of runs) and ceiling() takes max(c / n): the largest batch average.
Each stored run carries its own costUsd and judgeCostUsd (record keys: score, passed, turns, costUsd, judgeCostUsd, ...),
so the largest run is available and is 2.4x the largest mean today. Runs inside one batch differ a lot (one case's run
$0.83, another's a few cents), and the runs in flight when the tool trips can be the expensive ones, so the mean
understates exactly the quantity the subtraction is meant to cover. This breaks the front's decision 1 and leaves the
queue item's failing case (a ceiling passed by far at -j 4) open. The test fixture (2.4, 3), (4.0, 5) encodes the batch
mean, so it passes with the wrong rule.
Size: 15 minutes.
evidence: bin/paid-cost:45  per_run = max((c / n for c, n in records), default=None)
failing_case: The 10 stored records in ~/.relay/evals/relay: the largest single run costs $0.827 (costUsd + judgeCostUsd of one run in
2026-10-23T14-22-25Z-wt-structured-reword.json); the largest batch mean is $0.345. `bin/paid-cost ceiling --cap 4
--jobs 4` prints `4 2.97` (4 - 3 x 0.345). Four runs of $0.83 in flight when the tool trips at $2.97 end near $5.45,
well past the owner's $4. It should print `4 1.52` (4 - 3 x 0.827) by decision 1 ("the largest per-run cost measured
so far"), or -j 1 if the room is under one run.
fix_hint: Have stored() return the per-run costs (costUsd + judgeCostUsd of each run in cases[].arms[][]) alongside the batch
cost, and take ceiling's per_run as the max over all runs; update the fixture in tests to carry per-run costs.
pass_cases: 1. Records whose single runs cost 0.30, 0.80, 0.20 (batch of 3, costUsd 1.30): ceiling(cap 4, jobs 4) -> (4, 1.6),
computed from the 0.80 run, not from the 0.433 mean.
2. Same records, cap 1, jobs 4 -> (1, 1) (1 - 3 x 0.80 < 0.80).
3. Same records, cap 4, jobs 1 -> (1, 4).
4. No records -> (1, cap).
5. The real per-run cost is costUsd + judgeCostUsd of one run (a run with costUsd 0.70 and judgeCostUsd 0.12 counts as
0.82); a run with no numeric costUsd is skipped.
reason: tests/test_paid_cost_limits.py test_cap_minus_the_largest_run_not_the_mean, less_than_one_run, one_job, nothing_measured, run_cost_adds_judge_cost: pass, fail on old code
findings.summary: the ceiling subtracts the batch's mean cost per run, not the largest run measured, so the passed ceiling is still overshot

details: CONFIRMED by reading: default_dir() is $RELAY_HOME/evals/<repo>, which only bin/eval-record writes, and only bin/ci calls
it, for evals/plugin. Nothing stores judge-measure runs. So the README's recipe mixes eval sets, against decision 1's
"for that eval set", and the per-run costs of the two sets differ about 30-fold. The shown commands keep the
overshooting `-j 4 --max-cost-usd 10`, so the queue item's failing case ("the README's $10 ceiling can reach about
$13") is still there for anyone who copies the command.
Size: 15 minutes.
evidence: evals/judge-measure/README.md:23 "(`bin/paid-cost estimate` reads the stored batches of `bin/ci`, not these runs)"
failing_case: The README says: pass `bin/paid-cost ceiling --cap <your cap> --jobs 4` and use what it prints. bin/paid-cost reads
only $RELAY_HOME/evals/relay (the bin/ci plugin-eval batches, about $0.2-0.8 a run); judge-measure runs are never
stored there (the README itself says so a line above). Cap 10, jobs 4 prints `4 8.97` today, and `4 7.52` once F1 uses
the largest run, below the about $7.5-8 a full sonnet measurement costs, so the run stops partial and its tally says
NOT JUDGED. A judge-measure run costs about $0.026 (290 runs for about $7.5). And the two command lines just below still
read `-j 4 ... --max-cost-usd 10` and `--max-cost-usd 2`, so copying them gives the old overshoot (the $10 ceiling's
worst case of about $13). Decision 1: "the largest per-run cost measured so far for that eval set"; with no record of
that set it should be -j 1 and the cap, or a ceiling from judge-measure's own records.
fix_hint: Simplest: for judge-measure, say there is no stored record of these runs yet, so run with -j 1 and --max-cost-usd at
the cap (or give paid-cost a --dir for a judge-measure record folder); replace the -j 4 and fixed ceilings in the
command lines with <jobs> and <ceiling> from that.
pass_cases: 1. Artifact: the README's run instructions give a ceiling that comes from judge-measure's own runs, or, with none
stored, say to run with -j 1 and the cap itself; they do not point at the plugin evals' records.
2. Artifact: the two command lines do not hardcode `-j 4` together with a fixed `--max-cost-usd` that the text says can
be overshot; they use placeholders for the -j and the ceiling bin/paid-cost prints (or -j 1 and the cap).
3. If bin/paid-cost is given the eval set (e.g. --dir or --eval-set), `bin/paid-cost ceiling --cap 10 --jobs 4 --dir
<empty folder>` prints `1 10`.
reason: README lines 22-32 use -j 1 and placeholders, no plugin-eval records; test_empty_dir_prints_one_job_and_the_cap passes (pass case 3)
findings.summary: the judge-measure README sends the owner to a ceiling computed from the plugin evals' runs, another eval set, and still shows commands with -j 4 and fixed ceilings

details: CONFIRMED: stored() never reads the record's "partial" key (every stored record has it; all 10 today are false), and a
scratch fixture reproduces the low mean. A partial batch's cost is the ceiling's, not the batch's, so it is exactly
the "stopped at the ceiling" figure that made the old estimates low.
Size: 10 minutes.
evidence: $ python3 bin/paid-cost estimate --dir <scratch>/pc   (a.json full $9, b.json partial $2)
failing_case: Stored: one full batch of $9.00 and one batch with "partial": true that stopped at $2.00. `bin/paid-cost estimate`
prints "mean $5.50, max $9.00 over 2 stored runs"; it should print "not measured yet" (one full batch) or count only
full batches. bin/ci stores a partial record whenever the eval tool trips its ceiling (EVALS_MAX_COST=9 against $8.4-9.3
batches, as the plan's P-2 run used), so the next estimate drops.
fix_hint: In estimate (or stored), skip batch costs of records with partial true; keep their finished runs for the ceiling.
pass_cases: 1. Records: full $9.00, partial $2.00 -> estimate "not measured yet".
2. Records: full $9.00, full $8.00, partial $2.00 -> "mean $8.50, max $9.00 over 2 stored runs".
3. Records: full $6.00, full $8.00 -> "mean $7.00, max $8.00 over 2 stored runs" (today's test keeps passing).
4. A partial record's single runs still count for the ceiling's largest run (a run that finished has a real cost).
reason: test_partial_batch_is_not_counted and test_partial_batch_runs_count_for_the_ceiling pass, fail on old code
findings.summary: a partial batch (stopped at its ceiling) counts in the estimate as a full batch, pulling the mean down

details: CONFIRMED from the tool's help text. Behaviour follows decision 1; only the explanation is off, which matters when
someone sets a cap close to the money they have.
Size: 5 minutes.
evidence: --max-cost-usd <usd> ... The ceiling is checked before each run launches, so overrun is bounded to the runs in flight
failing_case: Docstring: "a ceiling can be passed by up to (jobs - 1) runs". `claude plugin eval --help`: "overrun is bounded to the
runs in flight (one, or up to --concurrency)". With -j 1 and a $4 cap, a batch can end at $4 + one run; with the
computed ceiling at -j 4, at cap + one run. The text should say the result stays within one run of the cap.
fix_hint: Reword the docstring line (and the bin/ci comment) to "up to one run per job; passing cap - (jobs - 1) x the largest run
keeps the batch within one run of the cap".
pass_cases: 1. Artifact: the docstring states the overrun bound as the runs in flight (up to jobs), and that the passed ceiling
keeps the batch within one run of the owner's cap.
2. ceiling() results unchanged by this wording fix.
reason: bin/paid-cost docstring and bin/ci comment reworded to one run per job, within one run of the cap
findings.summary: the docstring says a ceiling can be passed by up to (jobs - 1) runs; the eval tool says up to the runs in flight, i.e. up to jobs runs
